title: 1. Hook
content: Imagine traveling from a snowy mountain to a hot desert, and then to a place where it rains every day. Would you live in the same type of house everywhere? Let's explore a mystery: Why did a boy named Naseem see so many different types of houses at a camp in Srinagar?

title: 2. Socratic Thinking
content: If you had to build a house in a place where it rains all year round, how would you keep the water out? Would a normal flat-roofed house work? Why or why not?

content.title: 3. Discovery: Stilt Houses in Assam
content.description: Notice how the house is raised high above the ground on strong bamboo pillars. This keeps the inside dry even when the river floods.

title: 4. Reveal
content: The type of house we build depends on the climate (weather) and the materials available locally. In Assam, it rains heavily, so houses are built on bamboo stilts (10-12 feet high). In places like Manali where it snows, houses are made of stone or wood with sloping roofs.

description: A house built on elevated platforms or pillars (stilts), often over water or flood-prone land.
A roof that is angled so that rain and snow can slide off easily.

content: Emphasize to students that early humans didn't build houses; they adapted to caves. Today, we adapt our built environment to the local geography.

question: 5. Knowledge Check: Why are houses in Assam built on bamboo stilts?
options: To protect the house from heavy rain and floods
To keep the house warm in winter
To get a better view of the forest

content: Students often think igloos are cold inside. Explain that snow acts as an insulator, trapping body heat inside the igloo, keeping it warm.

title: 6. Reflection
content: Look at the roof of your own house. Is it flat or sloping? Talk to your parents about why your roof was built that way. What would happen if your roof was the opposite shape?

title: 7. Connection
content: Houses also depend on space and lifestyle. In crowded cities like Delhi, there is less land, so people build multi-storey buildings (flats) going up into the sky. Nomads, who travel often, live in temporary houses like tents.

title: 8. Mastery
content: Your challenge: Design a house for a desert where it is very hot during the day and very cold at night. Draw it, label the materials you would use, and explain how it will keep people comfortable.
